how: A member invites people to coordinate a logo effort in a Telegram group and two readers answer that they are in.
The member proposing the logo also posts its plan and receives explicit joining replies.
Two bare joining replies accept the logo proposal without asking for anything back.
The invitation receives two explicit bare acceptances, while any acceptance through silent placing remains unseen.
The starter combines proposing the mark and calling for participants in one post rather than two separate stages.
A participant proposes adding the product name because viewers may not recognise its icon.
An edited public update reports the circle, airplane and scripted fill complete while asking about expansion.
The building update reports scripted filling as complete and a later agreement proposes a bot for both images.
Scripts already appear in construction, while the later bot is a negotiated coexistence plan rather than demonstrated escalation caused by overwhelmed defenders.
Public reporting includes maintaining access to the coordination chat when a participant asks for an easier joining link.
Recruitment directs people into a separate chat while Reddit retains plans and status reports, requiring an explicit account of coordination across venues.
An invitation to a coordination chat and a staged plan cannot establish whether participants decided authority or divided responsibilities in the unseen conversation.
The coded record names a small location and step images but does not establish a pixel template or exact anchor coordinates within the cited concepts.
A proposed location and step images do not establish that a template resolved a design disagreement.
The edited completion report follows the invitation in the record but does not establish that the invitation caused construction.
A participant reports damage and requests repair, while another promises to protect the borders.
Reported completion is followed by a repair call identifying the existing logo as damaged, without identifying the damage source.
A willing repairer cannot continue maintenance once placement has ended, even while the original repair request remains visible.
A warning about overlap receives a border protection reply and develops into an explicitly confirmed compromise.
A visiting participant relays an earlier appeal to spare the logo and carries a compromise back into the thread.
The visitor apologises for possible overlap and reports attempts to stop advancing placers.
Apology and attempts to restrain placers precede the reported compromise, so restraint here cannot be attributed solely to a settled border.
Border negotiation concerns prospective sprite overlap, but the record does not identify that neighbour as the source of the separately reported damage.
The visitor anticipates that unread updates will undermine compliance, without anyone explicitly disputing the envoy's right to negotiate.
Concern about reaching placers is voiced before the compromise, so an agreement provoking a later dispute over representation is not demonstrated.
Making a workable agreement depends on reaching placers, and the proposed remedy is a bot preserving both images rather than universal obedience to updates.
The agreed plan would maintain both images through a bot, although actual cross-room placing remains unverified.
The compromise explicitly joins settlement of the overlap problem to a plan for maintaining both images.
A bilateral bot compromise does not establish a coalition, shared organisation or enduring alliance.
Questions about enlarging or adding a second logo do not document relocation after losing the first.
Describing border protection as inefficient while hoping two users suffice does not establish a judgement that the room lacks enough hands.
A local joke about images and text receives puzzlement and laughter without textual evidence that the canvas invitation itself was a prank.
Routing volunteers to a Telegram group establishes coordination elsewhere but does not establish host moderation or a rule containing canvas talk.
An invitation and subsequent joining-link exchange do not establish a canvas flood producing host boundary rules.
Participants credit the logo makers and congratulate their work both from within the effort and after arriving to praise it.
Completion and congratulations are both documented, but the edited update prevents a secure causal ordering of reported completion and the celebration post.
A reply explicitly marks the canvas as ended and the late repairer accepts that explanation.
A question about the icon's future is only a preliminary inquiry, so deciding what to keep must require evidence beyond asking what will happen.
A participant raises the icon's future before the close, but the record supplies no decision about what to keep.
The icon's future is queried but no preservation decision or continuation is visible in the cited exchanges.
A future-oriented question and acceptance of the ending provide no observed contest over cleaned images or the historical record.
Seeing the icon brings a visitor into the subreddit to praise it, adding a return from canvas visibility to room participation.
The ending is explained to a late repairer, but no cited passage makes prior celebration the reason for recording it.
The prospective question precedes the ending exchange and neither documents a preservation decision caused by recording the work.
The overlap warning concerns another group's placers and does not establish an attack organised by the host room.
The visitor is thanked and a compromise celebrated, while no cited exchange carries a rival contest through taunts or victory over the neighbour.
A logo effort and neighbour compromise supply no evidence that a prior rivalry named a canvas attack target.
